tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company has received a Show Cause Notice (SCN) from the Service Tax Department for the period April 2006 to March 2008, amounting to ₹ 6,348 Lacs, related to exports made to one of its customers.The Service Tax Department adjudicated in the Company's favor and dropped the demand of ₹ 6,348 Lacs. The Department filed an appeal against this decision with the Customs, Excise & Service Tax Appellate Tribunal (CESTAT), which was dismissed by the Hon'ble CESTAT in their order dated March 9, 2016. Subsequently, the Department filed an appeal against this order with the High Court on October 19, 2016, which is currently pending adjudication.
tax_litigation.status: Pending with High Court of Judicature at Bombay

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company had received demand notices from the Office of the Commissioner of Service Tax, for the period April 2008 to March 2010 on exports made to one of the customers of the Company. The company had recived similar notice from the Office of the Commissioner of Service Tax, for the period April 2006 to March,2008. On appeal to the Commissioner of Service Tax, the matter pertaining to the period April 2006 to March 2008 was adjudicated in favor of the Company The department had further filed an appeal against the said order with the Customs, Excise & Service Tax Appellate Tribunal (CESTAT) which was dismissed by the Hon’ble CESTAT vide their order dated March 9, 2016. On the same matter as aforesaid, the Company had received a Show Cause Notice (SCN) for the period April 2008 to March 2010 amounting to Rs. 28,97 lacs. The Company, in earlier years, with respect to the SCN's, submitted the replies to the Commissioner of Service tax on the same lines of the matter which was adjudicated in the Company's favor. The copy of the favorable CESTAT order has been submitted with Commissioner and SCN's are pending for adjudication as at the year-end.
tax_litigation.status: Pending with Commissioner of Service Tax

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company had received demand notices from the Office of the Commissioner of Service Tax, for the period April 2010 to March 2011 on exports made to one of the customers of the Company. The company had recived similar notice from the Office of the Commissioner of Service Tax, for the period April 2006 to March,2008. On appeal to the Commissioner of Service Tax, the matter pertaining to the period April 2006 to March 2008 was adjudicated in favor of the Company The department had further filed an appeal against the said order with the Customs, Excise & Service Tax Appellate Tribunal (CESTAT) which was dismissed by the Hon’ble CESTAT vide their order dated March 9, 2016. On the same matter as aforesaid, the Company had received a Show Cause Notice (SCN) for the period April 2010 to April 2011 amounting to Rs. 46 lacs. tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: With respect to Income Tax matters, a search was conducted on the Company's premises on 30 April 2013. Following this search, block assessments under section 153A of the Income-tax Act, 1961 (Act) were conducted for the Assessment Years 2007-08 to 2012-13. The Company did not appeal against the additions made in the assessment orders for these years. However, penalties were levied for these assessment years, which the Company challenged before the Income-tax Appellate Tribunal-Mumbai (ITAT). The Company accounted for the penalty amount as an exceptional item in the financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2018. Subsequently, the ITAT deleted the penalties levied, and the Income Tax Department refunded the penalties amounting to ₹1,044.44 Lacs along with interest of ₹138.33 Lacs under the Act to the Company. This was disclosed as an exceptional item in the financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2021 Following this, the Income Tax Department preferred an appeal before the Hon'ble High Court (HC) Bombay challenging the deletion of the penalties by the ITAT. This appeal is still in the pre-admission stage
tax_litigation.status: Pending for pre-admission at High Court of Judicature at Bombay

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company had received demand notices from the Office of the Deputy Commissioner of State Tax, Mumbai (Excluding Interest and penalty) pertaining to GST for the period April 2017 to March 2018 pertaining to alleged unreconciled turnover from Apple domestic subscriber revenue. The Company clarified that, as per the agreement with Apple, the responsibility for invoicing, collection, and discharge of GST on supplies to Indian subscribers rests with Apple, which has already paid the applicable GST. Supporting agreements and transaction details evidencing discharge of GST liability by Apple have also been submitted to the department. However officer has not accepted the submission and passed the order.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Deputy Commissioner of State Tax, Mumbai

Department alleged that company shall not avail ITC in respect to the shows that has been discontinued and written off in books. However company is in the view that being expenditure incurred in respect of production of shows and for the purpose of the business only therefore ITC shall be allowed.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Deputy Commissioner of State Tax, Mumbai

Company has availed all ITC from genuine vendors and has complied with conditions for availed of ITC.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Deputy Commissioner of State Tax, Mumbai

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company has received demand notices from the Office of the Deputy Commissioner of State Tax, Mumbai (excluding interest and penalty) pertaining to GST for the period April 2021 to March 2022, alleging excess outward tax liability as per GSTR-1 vis-à-vis GSTR-3B/GSTR-9 and excess ITC claimed in GSTR-3B as compared to GSTR-2A. The differences primarily arose due to incorrect reporting in GSTR-9 owing to the lack of clear guidelines prevailing at the relevant time. The management believes that the demand is not sustainable and expects the same to be deleted.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Deputy Commissioner of State Tax, Mumbai

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company has received demand notices from the Office of the Commissioner of CGST for the period April 2013 to June 2017, alleging non-payment of service tax on consideration received from the transfer of copyrights in sound recordings and related music rights to various music companies. The demand has been raised on the premise that such transfers constitute a temporary transfer of copyrights and are, therefore, liable to service tax. However, the Management is of the view that the said demand is not sustainable, as the copyrights were transferred on a perpetual basis and, accordingly, the transactions should not be subject to service tax.
